description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between the co-occurrence number (x-axis) and the accuracy (ACC, %) (y-axis) for six different methods—Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME—evaluated in the context of editing large language models for long-tail biomedical knowledge. The x-axis, labeled “Co-occurrence Number,” is displayed on a logarithmic scale ranging from 0 to approximately 10⁴, with major tick marks at 10⁰, 10¹, 10², and 10³. The y-axis, labeled “ACC (%)”, is linear and spans from 60% to 80%, with major gridlines at 60, 65, 70, 75, and 80. The “Base” method (black line with circle markers) starts at approximately 63% ACC at co-occurrence 1 and gradually increases to about 68% at 10⁴. “FT” (blue line with downward triangle markers) begins near 64.5% and rises to roughly 68.5%. “IKE” (red line with upward triangle markers) starts at ~66% and climbs to ~70%. “MEND” (brown line with diamond markers) begins at ~68% and reaches ~77%. “MEMIT” (purple line with pentagon markers) starts at ~68.5% and increases to ~75%. “ROME” (green line with square markers) begins at ~73.5% and steadily climbs to ~81.5% at the highest co-occurrence number. All methods show a positive trend in accuracy as co-occurrence number increases, with ROME consistently outperforming the others across the range.
